You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-e2484ef1: shift grid down one row

## Confirmed rule
Translate the entire input grid downward by exactly one row. Keep every cell in its original column and preserve its color. Fill the top row with the background color, and clip the original bottom row. Keep the grid dimensions unchanged.

## Demonstration
Input (3×3):
```
5 5 5
5 5 0
5 5 5
```
Output:
```
5 5 5
5 5 5
5 5 0
```
The lone 0 moves down one row; other cells remain background 5.

## Additional confirmed demonstration
A 23×2 demo used background 9 and sparse 0 cells. In 1-indexed coordinates, the input had zeros at (row 10, col 1), (11, 1), (12, 2), and (13, 2); the output had them at (11, 1), (12, 1), (13, 2), and (14, 2), with all other cells unchanged. This independently confirms a one-row downward translation of all cells, not an object-specific move or recoloring.

## Application and validation
For each future instance of this task, identify its background color from the grid, set output row 0 to that color, and copy input rows 0 through H−2 into output rows 1 through H−1. Discard any non-background content in the final input row rather than wrapping it. Preserve width and height; verify every output row has the same width as the input and compare each output row against the source row immediately above it.

Confirmed on a 4×11 test and the 23×2 demonstration above; a 15×30 instance was also accepted with the exact downward shift.
